title: Measure whether Qwen-Image-2.1 can paint and edit for Ask on a 64 GB Mac
goal: Find out, with numbers, whether the Qwen-Image-2.1 picture model is worth adding to Ask on this Mac: whether its see-through drawings beat today's drawings, whether it fits in memory beside the chat model, and whether it can edit a picture from a circle the person drew around the part to change. This is a measuring task: nothing ships to people from it, it ends in an audit and a recommendation.
notes:
The user, 2026-10-24, after a research pass on MOSS-Image and Qwen-Image-2.1 in the intake window: "file the qwen 2.1 measuring task". MOSS-Image was looked at and set aside (text-to-image only, several minutes a picture on a Mac in mflux, and its strength, words painted into a picture, is something Photonz already does better with live text layers).

What the research found (from web sources, NOT measured here):
- Qwen-Image-2.1 (Alibaba Qwen, 2026-09-20): 7.1B image model plus a Qwen3-VL 8B text encoder; generation and editing in one model; up to 10 reference images; edits marked by circles, painted marks or a mask; native RGBA; an 8 step Turbo; one ControlNet checkpoint (canny, depth, pose, scribble, lineart, ...) that also inpaints with --mask-image.
- mflux commands: mflux-generate-qwen-2.1, mflux-generate-qwen-2.1-edit (--image-paths), mflux-generate-qwen-2.1-controlnet (--controlnet-image-path, --mask-image), --model qwen-image-2.1-turbo, -q 8, --small-text-encoder (Qwen3.5 0.8B plus an adapter, about 2.1 GB, English prompts only, numerals in rendered text can be wrong, not with --auto-mask). See https://github.com/mflux-community/mflux/blob/main/src/mflux/models/qwen21/README.md
- Reported memory: bf16 about 46 GB peak; 8-bit about 27 to 31 GB peak because the 17.5 GB text encoder is never quantised; Turbo ControlNet 8-bit at 1024 about 45 s on an M5 Max. The Turbo model looks pixel-gridded below 1024.
- Licence: reported as the Qwen Research License (research and evaluation only, commercial use needs a separate licence from Qwen), unlike Z-Image's Apache 2.0. Verify from the model card.

Where it would plug in: the picture model setup is Sources/PhotonzCore/AskPictureModelPlan.swift (pinned packages, mflux==0.23.0 at line 73; fits() at line 57 uses AskModels.memoryShare = 0.6 in Sources/PhotonzCore/AskPlanning.swift:1245) and the server is Contents/Resources/PictureModel/server.py run by AskPictureServer; tracing is Scripts/picture-model/layers.py, whose backdrop clearing is what transparent output would replace. Design doc: docs/design/ask.md, 'Painting a drawing' and 'The picture model's setup'. Do the measuring in a separate scratch Python environment so the shipped picture-tools folder and its installed.txt are untouched.

Budget on 64 GB: 38.4 GB for models; the planning model holds 24.4 GB (27.6 peak), leaving about 14 GB, so 8-bit with the full encoder is expected NOT to fit beside it. That is a prediction to measure, not a fact.

Related, do not undo: ask-can-make-a-photo-as-well-as-an-illustration (seq 8) wants real photo layers; if this model is the better photo painter, say so in the audit for that task. settings-offers-several-ask-models-with-what-eac (seq 40) is where any extra picture model would be offered as a download. docs/design/separate-into-layers.md deliberately has no content-aware inpainting for Separate's patch fill; any editing this leads to belongs to Ask as an explicit request, never a silent change to Separate.
acceptance: The model runs through the mflux Photonz already sets up for its picture model (Settings > Ask), on an M4 Max 64 GB, beside the planning model Ask loads by default (Qwen3.8 27B); the mflux version used is named in the audit, and nothing changes the shipped picture model or its pinned package list

Memory is MEASURED for each way tried (8-bit with the full text encoder; 8-bit or 4-bit with mflux's --small-text-encoder; the planning model unloaded while painting) as resident GB held and at its peak, read the same way the Ask eval reads memory, and each is checked against Ask's rule that models together hold at most three fifths of the Mac (38.4 GB on 64 GB)
Time per picture is MEASURED at 768 and 1024 points for the Turbo (8 step) model and the base model, from a warm server and from a cold start, median of at least five

Drawings: the held-out drawing cases are run at Next defaults twice, once painted by Z-Image Turbo as today and once by Qwen-Image-2.1 asked for a transparent background, both traced into layers; the audit gives both scores per axis (didWhatWasAsked, clean, designed, crafted) and seconds per drawing request, and says whether transparent output really came back with an alpha channel (mflux notes say the edit decoder returns RGB only and only ControlNet output is RGBA: confirm or refute it)

Edits: at least eight edits on real screenshots and photos, each a picture plus a mark the person drew (a circle or painted stroke) plus a short instruction (for example circle a button and say make this blue; circle a person and say remove them), tried both with the mark painted on the picture and with a separate mask; the audit shows before and after pictures for each and says, per edit, whether pixels outside the marked area changed (MEASURED as mean pixel difference outside the mark)
The audit states the licence the weights come under and what it allows, quoting the licence text

The audit is at queue/audits/<date>-measure-qwen-image-2-1.json with a contact sheet of the drawings and the edits beside it, and ends in one recommendation: adopt for editing, adopt for drawing, offer as an extra download, or do not use, with the numbers that decide it
Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not

Adversarial pass before measuring: (1) mflux 0.23.0, the version Photonz pins, already ships Qwen-Image-2.1 (generate, edit with up to ten references, --mask-image, ControlNet); --small-text-encoder is NOT in any release, only mflux main since 2026-10-22 (commit 0fea52bada), so it is measured from a second scratch env and labelled unreleased. (2) The edit path quantises the text encoder too (q8 checkpoint 17 GB on disk: 8.8 text encoder, 7.1 transformer, 0.6 VAE), so the research's 27-31 GB peak for 8-bit (encoder never quantised) applies to the txt2img command, not the edit one. (3) ps resident size undercounts MLX's Metal buffers (5 GB shown vs 23 GB footprint at load from bf16), so memory is reported as the kernel's physical footprint (held and lifetime peak) beside the eval's ps reading. (4) The shipped server caps MLX's buffer cache at 1 GB; without that cap the footprint peaked at 53 GB, with it 30.9 GB, so every measurement uses the cap.

Baseline for drawings: held-out run 20261024-163432-ask-held-out (Qwen3.8 27B + MTP, Next defaults, Z-Image Turbo: total 57.8, drawing 64.4; drawing lines clean 5.9, designed 5.9, didWhatWasAsked 6.3, crafted 6.0; 155.3 s a drawing request). Only two commits touched Ask since (title bar Ask button, Command K on videos), neither touches drawing. A fresh baseline started 17:14 ran 3 cases per 8 minutes (about 2 h 20 for the set) and was stopped after 6 cases to give the Mac to the Qwen run; it is incomplete and not in the history.
